title: 'Add a test for #38383'
category: feature
requirement: 'This is regression-hardening work for an internal aggregate-function edge case. The objective is to keep current query behavior unchanged while eliminating the undefined-behavior pattern that shows up under sanitizers when nullable data flows through this code path. Users should see the same results as before, but the implementation should no longer rely on unsafe internal assumptions.

  '

title: Add ldapr to AArch64 server builds
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Teams running ClickHouse on modern AArch64 cloud hardware expect the server builds to take advantage of the architectural features that are commonly available on Graviton2-class and similar instances. Leaving out `ldapr` means heavily contended code paths and allocator workloads can miss performance that newer ARM systems should be able to deliver.


  ## Desired outcome

  AArch64 server builds that already target the newer ARM feature level should enable `ldapr` as part of the generated compiler feature set. This should improve performance on supported ARMv8.2+ environments without changing how unsupported or older architectures are built.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Modern AArch64 server binaries are built with `ldapr` enabled alongside the existing ARMv8.2 feature bundle, while non-AArch64 and older compatibility builds continue to follow their current paths. The change is performance-oriented and does not alter SQL behavior or user-facing interfaces.

  '

title: Add constexpr
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  This is internal C++ maintenance in aggregate-function code, and users should not observe any change in aggregate semantics just because compile-time constants are expressed more precisely.


  ## Desired outcome

  Introduce the compile-time cleanup needed here while keeping the runtime behavior, return values, and public aggregate contracts unchanged.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The code builds with the new constant-expression form, and aggregate behavior remains identical from a user''s point of view.

  '

title: ActionsDAG rename index to outputs
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  ClickHouse developers working on expression planning need internal graph terminology that reflects the current abstraction instead of older indexing language. This rename should improve readability without changing any user-visible query behavior.


  ## Desired outcome

  The internal `ActionsDAG` API should use `outputs` terminology consistently in place of the old `index` naming where that concept now represents produced nodes.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The affected interpreter and planning code compiles against the new terminology, and query results and planner behavior remain unchanged from a user perspective.

  '

item.text: The API confirms PRs are represented as merge commits on the main branch. I’m switching to a local upstream clone with commit metadata so I can bulk-resolve PR numbers to merge SHAs and avoid API rate limits.
The upstream metadata clone is in progress. Once it finishes, I’ll derive an ordered PR-to-merge-commit map and compare it to this snapshot so I can batch the replay safely.

The clone is taking a bit, which is expected for this repository even with blobs filtered out. I’m keeping it in the background and will use that metadata to automate the commit selection once it’s ready.

/bin/bash -lc "python3 - <<'PY'
import subprocess, re, json
from pathlib import Path
req_map=json.loads(Path('/workspace/requirements/.rename_map.json').read_text())
nums={int(k[:-5]): v[:-5] for k,v in req_map.items()}
log=subprocess.check_output(['git','-C','/tmp/ch-upstream-6000','log','--merges','--format=%H\\t%s']).decode()
pat=re.compile(r'"'^(?P<sha>[0-9a-f]+)'"\\tMerge pull request #(?P<num>\\d+) ')
found={}
for line in log.splitlines():
    m=pat.match(line)
    if not m: continue
    num=int(m.group('num'))
    if num in nums and num not in found:
        found[num]=m.group('sha')
print('requirements with merge commit found', len(found), 'of', len(nums))
missing=sorted(set(nums)-set(found))
print('first missing', missing[:30])
print('last missing', missing[-30:])
PY"

title: Add a comment
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Future maintainers working on table-function permissions need the readonly contract to be obvious from the code, because this area is easy to misinterpret.

  ## Desired outcome

  Keep behavior unchanged while documenting the non-obvious rule that governs when a table function may be allowed in readonly mode, so later changes do not regress that contract accidentally.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A reader of the interface can understand the readonly expectation without reverse-engineering earlier patches.

  '

title: Fix aspell
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Maintainers depend on ClickHouse’s spelling checks to catch real mistakes without failing on accepted product terms. The current aspell dictionary still contains incorrect or incomplete entries, which turns routine documentation work into avoidable style failures.


  ## Desired outcome

  The spelling allowlist should be corrected so docs and changelog contributions pass when they use the intended product vocabulary and still fail on genuine misspellings. This is a tooling-only cleanup.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The adjusted dictionary entries make aspell checks pass for the intended terms, and no SQL behavior, configuration surface, or operator-facing output changes.'

      "body": "### Changelog category (leave one):\r\n- Improvement\r\n\r\n### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md):\r\nImplement `ATTACH` of `MergeTree` table for `s3_plain` disk (plus some fixes for `s3_plain`)\r\n\r\nSimple example:\r\n\r\n```sql\r\n-- BACKUP writes Ordinary like structure\r\nset allow_deprecated_database_ordinary=1;\r\ncreate database ordinary engine=Ordinary;\r\n\r\ncreate table ordinary.test_backup_attach engine=MergeTree() order by tuple() as select * from numbers(100);\r\n-- NOTE: name of backup (\"backup\") is significant.\r\nbackup table ordinary.test_backup_attach TO Disk('backup_disk_s3_plain', 'backup');\r\n\r\ndrop table ordinary.test_backup_attach;\r\nattach table ordinary.test_backup_attach (number UInt64) engine=MergeTree() order by tuple() settings storage_policy='attach_policy_s3_plain';\r\n```\r\n\r\n<details>\r\n\r\n<summary>storage configuration</summary>\r\n\r\n```xml\r\n<clickhouse>\r\n    <storage_configuration>\r\n        <disks>\r\n            <backup_disk_s3_plain>\r\n                <type>s3_plain</type>\r\n                <endpoint>http://minio1:9001/root/data/disks/disk_s3_plain/</endpoint>\r\n                <access_key_id></access_key_id>\r\n                <secret_access_key></secret_access_key>\r\n            </backup_disk_s3_plain>\r\n            <attach_disk_s3_plain>\r\n                <type>s3_plain</type>\r\n                <!-- NOTE: /backup/ is a name of BACKUP -->\r\n                <endpoint>http://minio1:9001/root/data/disks/disk_s3_plain/backup/</endpoint>\r\n                <access_key_id></access_key_id>\r\n                <secret_access_key></secret_access_key>\r\n            </attach_disk_s3_plain>\r\n        </disks>\r\n        <policies>\r\n            <attach_policy_s3_plain>\r\n                <volumes>\r\n                    <main>\r\n                        <disk>attach_disk_s3_plain</disk>\r\n                    </main>\r\n                </volumes>\r\n            </attach_policy_s3_plain>\r\n        </policies>\r\n    </storage_configuration>\r\n    <backups>\r\n        <allowed_disk>backup_disk_s3_plain</allowed_disk>\r\n    </backups>\r\n</clickhouse>\r\n```\r\n\r\n</details>\r\n\r\nFollow-up for: #42232\r\nFixes: #42153 (cc @alexey-milovidov )\r\nRefs: #28527 (cc @filimonov )\r\n\r\n_P.S. Note, that this PR also includes some refactoring around metadata code, but everything is in a separate patch, hope this will help with review._",

      "body": "### Changelog category (leave one):\r\n- New Feature\r\n\r\n### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md):\r\nImplement schema inference for **row** freeform text format.\r\n\r\nCloses https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/34006\r\n\r\nOnce this is done you *should* be able to ingest arbitrary tabular text files (ie. application logs) without specifying the structure (Template).\r\n\r\n*Example usage:*\r\n\r\nRead data from file\r\n```sql\r\nSELECT * FROM file(<file_path>,'Freeform')\r\n```\r\n\r\nDescribe data from file\r\n```sql\r\nDesc file(<file_path>,'Freeform')\r\n```\r\n\r\n*How it is implemented*\r\n\r\n`FreeformFieldMatcher` houses an array of matchers that parse text data by escaping rules (JSON, CSV, Raw(but cutoff by whitespace), Quoted and Escaped).\r\n\r\nFirst, FreeformFieldMatcher will iterate over this set of matchers and generate as many solutions as possible.\r\n\r\nA `Solution` is defined as the order of the matchers to parse one row successfully associated with a score. The score here is generated by continuously adding the score of each field in the solution, specifically by the escaping rule and the type of the field. More specific fields (ie. DateTime) yield higher scores.\r\n\r\nFor now we only generate solutions for the first row because the data is supposed to be *tabular* to we *should* be able to get an acceptable solution just by looking at one row. Then the solutions are sorted by score and they are check against `max_rows_to_check`. The first solution matches all of the `max_rows_to_check` would be picked as the final solution.\r\n\r\nCurrently this works with CSV and syslog but more testing and tunings needs to be made for it to be in an acceptable state.\r\n\r\nFrom\r\n```csv\r\n1,2021-04-01 00:00:18,2021-04-01 00:21:54,1,8.40,1,N,79,116,1,25.5,3,0.5,5.85,0,0.3,35.15,2.5\r\n1,2021-04-01 00:42:37,2021-04-01 00:46:23,1,.90,1,N,75,236,2,5,3,0.5,0,0,0.3,8.8,2.5\r\n```\r\nwe have\r\n```\r\n1       2021    4       1       0       0       18      2021    4       1       0       21      54      1       8.4     1       N       79      116     1       25.5    3       0.5     5.85    0       0.3     35.15   2.5\r\n1       2021    4       1       0       42      37      2021    4       1       0       46      23      1       0.9     1       N       75      236     2       5       3       0.5     0       0       0.3     8.8     2.5\r\n```\r\n\r\nFrom\r\n```\r\nNov 13 10:29:56 Tri chronyd[227]: Selected source PHC0\r\nNov 13 13:24:02 Tri kernel: [91566.562562] hv_utils: TimeSync IC version 4.0\r\nNov 13 13:24:02 Tri chronyd[227]: Forward time jump detected!\r\n```\r\nwe have\r\n```\r\nNov     13      10      29      56      Tri     chronyd[227]:   Selected source PHC0\r\nNov     13      13      24      2       Tri     kernel: [91566.562562] hv_utils: TimeSync IC version 4.0\r\nNov     13      13      24      2       Tri     chronyd[227]:   Forward time jump detected!\r\n```\r\n\r\n\r\n*Update 2022-28-11:*\r\n\r\nWith the new changes on increasing the search tree size, we now iterate over all matchers and don't exit early. However, a new field is added only if it has a better type score than the previous field or if no field other than type string has been found. This helps us to better parse the previous CSV example:\r\n\r\n```\r\n1       2021-04-01      0       0       18      2021-04-01      0       21      54      1       8.4     1       N       79      116     1       25.5    3       0.5     5.85    0       0.3     35.15   2.5\r\n1       2021-04-01      0       42      37      2021-04-01      0       46      23      1       0.9     1       N       75      236     2       5       3       0.5     0       0       0.3     8.8     2.5\r\n```\r\n\r\nAnd also ClickHouse's logs:\r\n\r\n```\r\n2022-11-17      11      7       30.825405       [395843]        {345bf223-db80-4772-9a07-73542321e715::202211_15349_15604_53}   <Debug> MergeTask::PrepareStage:        Merging 6 parts: from 202211_15349_15599_52 to 202211_15604_15604_0 into Compact\r\n2022-11-17      11      7       30.826372       [395843]        {345bf223-db80-4772-9a07-73542321e715::202211_15349_15604_53}   <Debug> MergeTask::PrepareStage:        Selected MergeAlgorithm: Horizontal\r\n```\r\n\r\n*Update 2022-30-12:*\r\n\r\nNow we could parse and unmarshal JSON object fields into their own columns.\r\n*TODO:* \r\n- Make use of the SchemaCache to store the solution\r\n- Fix the new added test",

      "body": "### Changelog category (leave one):\r\n- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in official stable or prestable release)\r\n\r\n### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md):\r\nFixed race condition between inserts and dropping MVs\r\n\r\nA race condition happened when a Materialized View was dropped at the same time as an INSERT, where the MVs was present as a dependency of the insert at the beggining of the execution, but the table has been dropped by the time the Insert Chain tries to access to it, producing either an UNKNOWN_TABLE or TABLE_IS_DROPPED exception, and stopping the Insertion.\r\nI have added a couple of checks to avoid these exceptions and just continue with the insert if the dependency is gone. \r\n",

      "body": "### Changelog category (leave one):\r\n- New Feature\r\n\r\n### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md):\r\nAdd `extractKeyValuePairs` function to extract key value pairs from strings. Input strings might contain noise (i.e log files / do not need to be 100% formatted in key-value-pair format), the algorithm will look for key value pairs matching the arguments passed to the function. As of now, function accepts the following arguments: `data_column` (mandatory), `key_value_pair_delimiter` (defaults to `:`), `pair_delimiters` (defaults to `\\space \\, \\;`) and `quoting_character` (defaults to double quotes).\r\n\r\nThe `extractKeyValuePairsWithEscaping` has also been added and it has escape sequences support built-in. Supported escape sequences are the same as the ones supported by `DB::parseComplexEscapeSequence` as it is used to parse them.\r\n\r\nExamples:\r\n\r\n**Simple case**\r\n``` sql\r\narthur :) select extractKeyValuePairs('name:neymar, age:31 team:psg,nationality:brazil') as kv\r\n\r\nSELECT extractKeyValuePairs('name:neymar, age:31 team:psg,nationality:brazil') as kv\r\n\r\nQuery id: f9e0ca6f-3178-4ee2-aa2c-a5517abb9cee\r\n\r\n┌─kv──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\r\n│ {'name':'neymar','age':'31','team':'psg','nationality':'brazil'}        │\r\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\r\n```\r\n\r\n**Single quote as quoting character**\r\n``` sql\r\narthur :) select extractKeyValuePairs('name:\\'neymar\\';\\'age\\':31;team:psg;nationality:brazil,last_key:last_value', ':', ';,', '\\'') as kv\r\n\r\nSELECT extractKeyValuePairs('name:\\'neymar\\';\\'age\\':31;team:psg;nationality:brazil,last_key:last_value', ':', ';,', '\\'') as kv\r\n\r\nQuery id: 0e22bf6b-9844-414a-99dc-32bf647abd5e\r\n\r\n┌─kv───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\r\n│ {'name':'neymar','age':'31','team':'psg','nationality':'brazil','last_key':'last_value'}                                 │\r\n└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\r\n```\r\n\r\n**Escape sequences without escape sequences support**\r\n``` sql\r\narthur :) select extractKeyValuePairs('age:a\\\\x0A\\\\n\\\\0') as kv\r\n\r\nSELECT extractKeyValuePairs('age:a\\\\x0A\\\\n\\\\0') AS kv\r\n\r\nQuery id: e9fd26ee-b41f-4a11-b17f-25af6fd5d356\r\n\r\n┌─kv────────────────────┐\r\n│ {'age':'a\\\\x0A\\\\n\\\\0'} │\r\n└───────────────────────┘\r\n```\r\n**Escape sequences with escape sequence support turned on**\r\n``` sql\r\narthur :) select extractKeyValuePairsWithEscaping('age:a\\\\x0A\\\\n\\\\0') as kv\r\n\r\nSELECT extractKeyValuePairsWithEscaping('age:a\\\\x0A\\\\n\\\\0') AS kv\r\n\r\nQuery id: 44c114f0-5658-4c75-ab87-4574de3a1645\r\n\r\n┌─kv───────────────┐\r\n│ {'age':'a\\n\\n\\0'} │\r\n└──────────────────┘\r\n```\r\n\r\n\r\n**Implementation design**:\r\n\r\nInput string is processed by a state machine, see `CHKeyValuePairExtractor` and `StateHandlerImpl`.\r\n\r\nIf escaping support is off, there is no temporary copies of possible keys and values. `std::string_view` is used to store references and later on they are inserted directly into the output column. If escaping support is on, possible keys and values are copied directly into the output columns. If those turn out to be invalid keys/ values, they are discarded without de-allocating the memory used by them. Check `NoEscapingStateHandler::StringWriter` and `InlineEscapingStateHandler::StringWriter` for reference.\r\n\r\nSSE42 and SSE2 are used for string search when available on the system. For that, runtime versions of `find_first_symbols` had to be added to `base/find_symbols` as the needles/ symbols to be searched for are not known at compile time.\r\n\r\n**Functional (user perspective) differences between previous implementation (last reviewed) and current implementation**\r\n\r\n1. Order of input parameters have changed.\r\n2. No more `special_value_characters_allowlist`.\r\n3. As long as a character is not a control character it's considered valid, as opposed to previous implementation where only alphanum was considered non-special and everything else had to be escaped. In pratice, that means !@#$%¨&*( and other \"special\" characters will be considered valid part of keys and values unless specified in control characters.\r\n4. Default escape sequences are now transformed into their corresponding values (e.g \\n -> 0xA).\r\n5. Non default escape sequences are now returned as it is (e.g \\\\$ -> \\\\$).\r\n6. There can be multiple pair delimiters as opposed to only one. By default \\space is one of them, which means `name :arthur` will not output anything because it has found a pair delimiter where it is not supposed to. If space is removed from delimiters, the output key will include the trailing space.\r\n7. Escape character is no longer configurable, it's hardcoded to `\\`.\r\n \r\n\r\nCloses https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/41009\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n> Information about CI checks: https://clickhouse.com/docs/en/development/continuous-integration/\r\n",

      "body": "<!---\r\nA technical comment, you are free to remove or leave it as it is when PR is created\r\nThe following categories are used in the next scripts, update them accordingly\r\nutils/changelog/changelog.py\r\ntests/ci/run_check.py\r\n-->\r\n### Changelog category (leave one):\r\n- Improvement\r\n\r\n\r\n### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md):\r\nImprove internal S3 client to correctly deduce regions and redirections for different types of URLs.\r\n\r\n\r\nI defined a client that will try to detect region for the endpoint (if it's not explicitly defined in the URL or config) by using `HeadBucket` allowing us to use `HeadObject` correctly.\r\nRegions will be cached for each bucket per client.\r\n\r\nAdditionally, I noticed that the SDK doesn't handle correctly code 301 when the style of URL changes.\r\nFor example, this never worked with CH:\r\n```\r\nSELECT * FROM s3('https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-public-datasets/wikistat/partitioned/wikistat201801.native.zst') limit 10\r\n```\r\nbecause redirect is to a different style URL (virtual address) while AWS SDK simply changes URI authority with the location in the body.\r\nI defined a similar logic with cache as for the region and now this also correctly works, even with `HeadObject`.\r\n\r\nTo verify that both caches are working, you can define an S3 table and check the performance difference between first and second run (if an URL without region is used and even more if it's redirected).\r\n\r\nThings left to do:\r\n\r\n- [x] go through the code and try to include it in other places (e.g. BackupS3)\r\n- [x] see if tests are happy with the changes\r\n- [x] add `SYSTEM DROP S3 CLIENT CACHE`\r\n\r\nAWS SDK PR https://github.com/ClickHouse/aws-sdk-cpp/pull/13\r\n\r\n### Documentation entry for user-facing changes\r\n\r\n- [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features)\r\n\r\n<!---\r\nDirectly edit documentation source files in the \"docs\" folder with the same pull-request as code changes\r\n\r\nor\r\n\r\nAdd a user-readable short description of the changes that should be added to docs.clickhouse.com below.\r\n\r\nAt a minimum, the following information should be added (but add more as needed).\r\n- Motivation: Why is this function, table engine, etc. useful to ClickHouse users?\r\n\r\n- Parameters: If the feature being added takes arguments, options or is influenced by settings, please list them below with a brief explanation.\r\n\r\n- Example use: A query or command.\r\n-->\r\n\r\n\r\n> Information about CI checks: https://clickhouse.com/docs/en/development/continuous-integration/\r\n",

      "body": "<!---\r\nA technical comment, you are free to remove or leave it as it is when PR is created\r\nThe following categories are used in the next scripts, update them accordingly\r\nutils/changelog/changelog.py\r\ntests/ci/run_check.py\r\n-->\r\n### Changelog category (leave one):\r\n\r\n- Improvement\r\n\r\n\r\n### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md):\r\nresolve issue #38075 . Right now async insert doesn't support deduplication, because multiple small inserts will coexist in one part, which corespond multiple `block id`s. This solution is straitfoward: \r\nThe change involves:\r\n1. mark offsets for every inserts in every chunk\r\n2. calculate multiple `block_id`s when sinker receive a chunk\r\n3. get block number lock by these `block_id`s\r\n  3.1. if fails, remove the dup insert(s) and dup `block_id`(s) from block and recalculate `offsets` agian.\r\n  3.2. if succeeds, commit `block_id`'s and other items into keeper\r\n    a. if fails, do 3.1\r\n    b. if succeeds, everything succeeds\r\n\r\n> Information about CI checks: https://clickhouse.com/docs/en/development/continuous-integration/\r\n",

      "body": "Algorithm is divided into 2 steps:\r\n\r\n1. Partition compatibility check;\r\n2. Clone parts and update files;\r\n\r\n**Partition compatibility check**\r\nIn order for 2 partition expressions to be considered compatible, they must meet one of the following:\r\n1. Destination partition expressions must be a subset of source partition expressions; or\r\n2. Destination partition expression must be monotonically increasing in the source partition min max range.\r\n\r\nMonotonicity check does not work for functions with more than 1 variable argument. Therefore, it is a must that all expressions in the partition expression contain at most 1 variable argument.\r\n\r\n**Clone**\r\n\r\n1. Hard link all files as usual.\r\n2. Delete/ unlink checksums.txt, partition.dat and minmax_<partition_exp_columns>.idx (dst table only).\r\n3. Recalculate those files and write them back in the destination folder.\r\n4. Do rest as usual.\r\n\r\n### Changelog category (leave one):\r\n- New Feature\r\n\r\n### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md):\r\nAllow partitions from tables with different partition expressions to be attached when the destination table partition expression doesn't re-partition/ split the part.\r\n\r\nCloses #13826\r\n\r\n> Information about CI checks: https://clickhouse.com/docs/en/development/continuous-integration/\r\n",

      "body": "- introducing simple mock for S3 client\r\n  - it tests in sync and async mode\r\n  - injecting errors\r\n- some tests for part splitting in multi part upload\r\n- less copy operation inside WriteBufferFromS3 due to attaching memory to the iostream\r\n- test for limiting part size for task:\r\n  - https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/44271\r\n  - buffer could produce parts >5G, would be generated 5G + 1m parts.\r\n- simplify task synchronization\r\n\r\nOther thing related to the topic, deserve to be as separate issues,\r\n- limit active tasks count by memory size in allocated buffers\r\n- DO NOT CALL finalize inside destructors (WriteIndirectBufferFromRemoteFS, WriteBufferFromFileDecorator) within no-throw scope. That breaks the contract with, for example, WriteBufferFromS3. A file is written to S3 only when finalize has finished successfully.       "body": "Resoves #19970\r\nResolves #37216\r\n\r\nA (generalized) inverted index for ClickHouse developed by @HarryLeeIBM and @larryluogit\r\n\r\nThis inverted index is implemented as a new type of skipping index. The implementation is well-aligned with ClickHouse's secondary/skipping index architecture, including index creation/alter/drop syntax, block stream piping, expression (RPN) evaluation, etc.\r\n\r\nTo define a GIN index:\r\n```sql\r\nCREATE TABLE my_table1 (k UInt64,s String,INDEX my_gin_index(s) TYPE inverted(0) GRANULARITY 1)  Engine=MergeTree ORDER BY (k)\r\nCREATE TABLE my_table2 (k UInt64,s String,INDEX my_gin_index(s) TYPE inverted(3) GRANULARITY 1)  Engine=MergeTree ORDER BY (k)\r\n```\r\n\r\n`gin()` (or `gin(0)`) set the tokenizer to \"tokens\", whereas `gin(n)` with `n` between `2` and `8` sets \"ngrams(n)” as tokenizer.\r\n\r\nMain implementation techniques include, Roaring Bitmap(for postings lists) and FST(for term dictionaries), see the following references:\r\n1. Single-pass index construction with segmentation, see Heinz, Steffen, and Justin Zobel. 2003. [Efficient single-pass index construction for text databases](https://doi.org/10.1002/asi.10268). JASIST 54(8):713–729.\r\n2. Roaring Bitmaps, see https://github.com/RoaringBitmap/RoaringBitmap\r\n3. Finite State Transducer (FST) Minimization, see Mihov, S., Maurel, D. (2001). [Direct Construction of Minimal Acyclic Subsequential Transducers](https://doi.org/10.1007/3-540-44674-5_18). In: Yu, S., Păun, A. (eds) Implementation and Application of Automata. CIAA 2000. Lecture Notes in Computer Science, vol 2088. Springer, Berlin, Heidelberg. \r\n\r\nA merge tree setting exists to control the maximum size of data digestion during indexing: `max_digestion_size_per_segment` (default is 256M).\r\n\r\nThe following steps demonstrate the inverted index feature using hackernews dataset.\r\n1. Create and load hackernews table\r\n\r\n```sql\r\nCREATE TABLE hackernews ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id\r\n          AS SELECT * FROM url('https://datasets.clickhouse.com/hackernews.native.zst', Native,\r\n          $$\r\n          id UInt32,\r\n          deleted UInt8,\r\n          type Enum('story' = 1, 'comment' = 2, 'poll' = 3, 'pollopt' = 4, 'job' = 5),\r\n          by LowCardinality(String),\r\n          time DateTime,\r\n          text String,\r\n          dead UInt8,\r\n          parent UInt32,\r\n          poll UInt32,\r\n          kids Array(UInt32),\r\n          url String,\r\n          score Int32,\r\n          title String,\r\n          parts Array(UInt32),\r\n          descendants Int32\r\n          $$);\r\n```\r\n\r\n2. Create hackernews_gin3 table, which has the same column definitions as hackernews but with an inverted index.\r\n```sql\r\nSET allow_experimental_inverted_index = 1;\r\n\r\nCREATE TABLE hackernews_gin3\r\n(\r\n          id UInt32,\r\n          deleted UInt8,\r\n          type Enum('story' = 1, 'comment' = 2, 'poll' = 3, 'pollopt' = 4, 'job' = 5),\r\n          by LowCardinality(String),\r\n          time DateTime,\r\n          text String,\r\n          dead UInt8,\r\n          parent UInt32,\r\n          poll UInt32,\r\n          kids Array(UInt32),\r\n          url String,\r\n          score Int32,\r\n          title String,\r\n          parts Array(UInt32),\r\n          descendants Int32,\r\n          INDEX inverted(text) TYPE gin(3) GRANULARITY 1\r\n) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id\r\nSETTINGS index_granularity=1024;\r\n```\r\n\r\n3. Populate hackernews_gin3 table by copying the same data from hackernews table\r\n```sql\r\nset max_insert_threads=6;\r\ninsert into hackernews_gin3 select * from hackernews;\r\n```\r\n\r\n4. Run query against hackernews and hackernews_gin3 for comparison\r\n```sql\r\nSELECT * FROM hackernews WHERE text LIKE '%I love clickhouse%';\r\nSELECT * FROM hackernews_gin3 WHERE text LIKE '%I love clickhouse%';\r\n```\r\n\r\n### Changelog category (leave one):\r\n- New Feature\r\n\r\n### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md):\r\nAdd an experimental inverted index as a new secondary index type for efficient text search.\r\n\r\n### Documentation entry for user-facing changes\r\n- [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features)",

      "body": "### Changelog category (leave one):\r\n- Improvement\r\n\r\n### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md):\r\nReplace back `clickhouse su` command with `sudo -u` in start in order to respect limits in `/etc/security/limits.conf`.\r\n\r\n----\r\nLimits configured in `/etc/security/limits.d` are not respected by `clickhouse su` command. See below. Propose to revert back to old command and use new command only in docker-related stuff as intended.\r\n\r\n```\r\nroot@localhost.com:~# sudo -u clickhouse /bin/bash -c \"ulimit -Hn\"\r\n1048576\r\nroot@localhost.com:~# /usr/bin/clickhouse su clickhouse /bin/bash -c \"ulimit -Hn\"\r\n1048576\r\nroot@localhost.com:~#\r\nroot@localhost.com:~# ulimit -n 10500\r\nroot@localhost.com:~# ulimit -Hn\r\n10500\r\nroot@localhost.com:~# sudo -u clickhouse /bin/bash -c \"ulimit -Hn\"\r\n1048576\r\nroot@localhost.com:~# /usr/bin/clickhouse su clickhouse /bin/bash -c \"ulimit -Hn\"\r\n10500\r\nroot@localhost.com:~#\r\n\r\nroot@localhost.com:~# cat /etc/security/limits.d/*\r\nclickhouse soft nofile 1048576\r\nclickhouse hard nofile 1048576\r\nwww-data soft nofile 102400\r\nwww-data hard nofile 102400\r\nmysql soft nofile 1048576\r\nmysql hard nofile 1048576\r\nmysql soft memlock -1\r\nmysql hard memlock -1\r\nroot soft nofile 1048576\r\nroot hard nofile 1048576\r\nroot soft memlock -1\r\nroot hard memlock -1\r\n* soft nofile 1048576\r\n* hard nofile 1048576\r\n* soft memlock -1\r\n* hard memlock -1\r\nroot@localhost.com:~#\r\n```",

      "body": "### Changelog category (leave one):\r\n- New Feature\r\n\r\n### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md):\r\nIntroduce non-throwing variants of hasToken and hasTokenCaseInsensitive\r\n\r\n### Documentation entry for user-facing changes\r\n\r\n- [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features)\r\n\r\nSince the `hasToken` function isn't explicitly documented in the first place, I'll provide some explanation below:\r\n- Motivation: Providing the means to handle queries potentially containing an illegal `needle` parameter by returning `null` instead of throwing an exception.\r\n- Parameters: `haystack` as first argument and `needle` as second, matching that of `hasToken`.\r\n- Example use:\r\n```\r\n:) select hasTokenOrNull('asdf', 'asdf.ghjk');\r\nSELECT hasTokenOrNull('asdf', 'asdf.ghjk')\r\n\r\nQuery id: ba232cb4-ff65-432a-b95a-73ae7d76bd8b\r\n\r\n┌─hasTokenOrNull('asdf', 'asdf.ghjk')─┐\r\n│                                     ᴺᵁᴸᴸ │\r\n└──────────────────────────────────────────┘\r\n\r\n1 row in set. Elapsed: 0.007 sec.\r\n```\r\n",

import json, urllib.request, sys
from pathlib import Path
root=Path('/workspace')
req_dir=root/'requirements'
out_dir=root/'requirement_patches'
out_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
rename=json.loads((req_dir/'.rename_map.json').read_text())
slug_to_pr={v[:-5]: int(k[:-5]) for k,v in rename.items()}
slug_to_pr.update({
    '22-11-1-1360-changelog': 43349,
    '22-8-9-24-changelog': 43393,
    'aspell-dictionary-corrections': 44090,
    'post-release-version-bump-5': 43348,
    'readonly-table-function-comment': 43403,
})
slugs=sorted(p.stem for p in req_dir.glob('*.yaml'))
headers={'User-Agent':'codex-agent'}
for idx,slug in enumerate(slugs,1):
    pr=slug_to_pr.get(slug)
    if pr is None:
        raise SystemExit(f'missing PR mapping for {slug}')
    url=f'https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/{pr}.diff'
    req=urllib.request.Request(url, headers=headers)
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as resp:
        data=resp.read()
    path=out_dir/f'{slug}.diff'
    path.write_bytes(data)
    if path.stat().st_size == 0:
        raise SystemExit(f'empty diff for {slug} from PR {pr}')
    if idx % 50 == 0 or idx == len(slugs):
        print(f'{idx}/{len(slugs)}', file=sys.stderr)
print('done', len(slugs))
PY"

title: Add ldapr to AArch64 server builds
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Teams running ClickHouse on modern AArch64 cloud hardware expect the server builds to take advantage of the architectural features that are commonly available on Graviton2-class and similar instances. Leaving out `ldapr` means heavily contended code paths and allocator workloads can miss performance that newer ARM systems should be able to deliver.


  ## Desired outcome

  AArch64 server builds that already target the newer ARM feature level should enable `ldapr` as part of the generated compiler feature set. This should improve performance on supported ARMv8.2+ environments without changing how unsupported or older architectures are built.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Modern AArch64 server binaries are built with `ldapr` enabled alongside the existing ARMv8.2 feature bundle, while non-AArch64 and older compatibility builds continue to follow their current paths. The change is performance-oriented and does not alter SQL behavior or user-facing interfaces.

  '
